text: Harbour City 2-4 Seabrook Town: Trotz einer frühen 2:0-Führung von Harbour City durch Elias Okafor und Marek Barros, die aus ziemlich unwahrscheinlichen Chancen (xG 0.111 und 0.009) erzielten, drehte Seabrook Town das Spiel [#905] [#975]. Mit mehr Schüssen (22 zu 10) und deutlich höherem xG von 3.48 – das heißt, sie hatten viel mehr gute Torchancen – kam Seabrook zurück ins Spiel. Besonders Kian Romano war entscheidend und erzielte zwei Tore in der Nachspielzeit (90+2' und 90+3'), was das Comeback perfekt machte [#1882] [#1906]. Seabrook Town stellte nach Rückstand ihr Spiel um und setzte auf mehr Druck und direkte Pässe, was ihnen den späten Erfolg brachte [#1361]. Marek Barros überzeugte mit vielen Ballgewinnen und vorbereiteten Chancen, konnte die Niederlage aber nicht verhindern.

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for fan audience in de

- Seabrook Town won the match 4-2 despite trailing 2-0 early on [#905, #975, #1104, #1448, #1882, #1906].  
- Kian Romano scored twice in stoppage time (90+2' and 90+3') to secure Seabrook Town's comeback win [#1882, #1906].  
- Harbour City led 2-0 at 47' with goals by Elias Okafor and Marek Barros, both low xG chances (0.111 and 0.009) [#905, #975].  
- Seabrook Town had significantly higher xG (3.48) and more shots (22 vs. 10) across the match, reflecting their dominance [team_stats].  
- Marek Barros was Man of the Match with 1 goal, 2 assists, 9 interceptions, and a 9.8 rating despite his team losing [player_of_the_match].

- Seabrook Town scored three late goals (90+2', 90+3'), reflecting a decisive counter-attack pattern following regains of possession. The goal at 90+2' by Kian Romano came after a quick 6.7s buildup from regain with only 2 passes, indicating fast transition exploiting Harbour City’s advanced positioning [1881,1882]. The following goal at 90+3' involved a short passing move, showing efficient exploitation of space created by quick progression after turnover [1905,1906].

- Harbour City played in a 4-2-3-1 formation with a patient short passing style aiming to control possession and build attacks slowly, demonstrated by their opening goal at 45' constructed through a long buildup of 17 passes over 56.7 seconds [904,905]. This style created an early lead (2-0 after 47’) but may have made them vulnerable to fast counters.

- Seabrook Town’s 3-4-3 formation with wide crossing play style led to multiple set-piece and wide attacking opportunities, as seen in their several corners (9) and a direct cross assist by Marek Barros (Harbour City) on their second goal, showing varied crossing usage [975].

- After falling behind 2-0, Seabrook Town adapted tactically at 65’ to press higher and play more direct with increased line height, press intensity, and directness. This change correlates with their surge in chances and eventual comeback goals, showing a switch from possession-based play to high pressing and direct attacks to overwhelm Harbour City’s defensive structure [1361].

- Harbour City’s patient style reflected in their steady possession (46.6%) and high pass accuracy (81.8%) but lower field tilt (42.3%) indicates they had less territorial dominance, which Seabrook Town exploited especially after tactical shift by pressing more aggressively (PPDA dropping from 7.6 to 5.5 for Seabrook Town). The high turnovers for Seabrook (25) show their high-risk pressing game but also led to their usable ball recoveries and fast breaks [team_stats].
